summary: The 21st Muang Thai–Chiang Mai Marathon is confirmed for Sunday 20 December 2026. Choose this as a trip anchor if racing matters to you; casual visitors can enjoy the start-area atmosphere, but the pre-dawn schedule makes it a deliberate outing. The 10 km or 3 km offers simpler city logistics than the point-to-point longer races.
whyGo: Run from landmark Tha Phae Gate in an international event celebrating Chiang Mai’s 730th anniversary.
Choose among marathon, half-marathon, 10 km and 3 km distances; the organiser describes the courses as flat.
bestFor: Trained runners combining a race with a northern Thailand holiday.
Families choosing the 3 km Smile Run or children’s category.
skipIf: You want a relaxed late breakfast or cannot manage a very early start.
Your itinerary leaves no recovery time after a longer race.
duration: Allow the morning plus recovery. Cutoffs: marathon seven hours, half-marathon 3.5 hours, 10 km 90 minutes; add staging and transport.
cost: Foreign-entry regular fees through 31 October: marathon THB1,500; half THB1,200; 10 km THB700; 3 km THB600; children THB500. November and December tiers rise; processing charges are extra. Thai-national prices differ.
hours: 20 December: marathon 03:00, half 04:00, 10 km 05:00, 3 km 05:20. Expo/bib collection: 18–19 December, 10:00–18:00.
bestTime: Arrive in Chiang Mai by 18 December if practical, allowing collection and a quiet evening before racing.
gettingThere: Start at Tha Phae Gate on the Old City’s eastern edge. Consider accommodation within walking distance and confirm overnight transport beforehand. Marathon and half finish at King Naresuan Monument, Mae Rim; free return shuttles operate 06:30–10:30. Shorter races finish at the gate.
booking: Use the official site’s Jog & Joy registration link. Passport details identify foreign entries. Collect your pack before race day; fees are non-refundable. Check current availability before committing travel.
accessibility: Wheelchair participation, accessible toilets and shuttle access are not confirmed. Ask the organiser about individual requirements before entering.
practicalTips: Leave the following afternoon flexible for food, rest and delayed transport.
Check bag-transfer arrangements carefully: long-distance bags travel to a different finish.
Supporters should agree a meeting point and avoid assuming the long races return to the gate.
decemberNotes: This is the December city marathon, distinct from the university-branded CMU event. Expect a cool early start, but the organiser’s advertised 12–18°C is not a forecast. Recheck weather and final runner instructions close to departure.
uncertainties: Live remaining bib inventory, final road closures and accessible facilities were not established.
Historical event photography illustrates atmosphere, not the 2026 staging.
